reasoning:
The defect is real and correctly characterized. Two distinct sub-issues exist in utils.py:

1. URL construction (lines 51-56): `version = duckdb.__version__` is assigned verbatim and used directly in `https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/download/v{version}/libduckdb-osx-universal.zip`. No normalization (strip post/dev/local segments) occurs anywhere in the file or elsewhere in the package. If `duckdb.__version__` ever carries a PEP-440 local-version or post-release suffix (e.g. `1.3.2.post1`), the constructed tag `v1.3.2.post1` will not exist on GitHub and `urlopen` will raise an HTTPError 404 with no diagnostic pointing to the version mismatch.

2. Cache directory (lines 19-21): `_LIBDUCKDB_CACHE_DIR` is keyed on the same raw `duckdb.__version__` string, so any suffix would also create a non-standard cache path.

3. Homebrew ABI (lines 44-46): `_find_standalone_libduckdb` returns the first existing homebrew path (`/opt/homebrew/lib/libduckdb.dylib` or `/usr/local/lib/libduckdb.dylib`) without any version assertion. A user with homebrew duckdb 1.2.x and pip duckdb 1.3.2 would silently load a mismatched native library. The only check applied after loading is `_has_capi_symbols` (line 30), which only tests for `duckdb_open`—a symbol present across many versions—so the ABI mismatch is not caught.

Counterarguments considered and rejected:
- DuckDB PyPI releases (1.3.2, 1.4.x, 1.5.x) have historically used clean semver without post/dev suffixes, making the URL-404 scenario low-probability in practice. But the constraint `duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6` does not exclude post/dev builds and provides no guarantee going forward.
- The download path is a macOS-only, last-resort fallback (gated by user confirmation or env var), reducing real-world exposure further.

Severity 'low' is appropriate: the code-level defect is genuine and unambiguous, the homebrew ABI mismatch is a realistic edge case, but both are narrow failure modes on a rarely-exercised fallback path. No correction to severity is warranted.
